analysis.title: 10/22 Mkt Internal Insight: Systematic Selling Could be Violent but Short-Lived (a day or two)
key_insights: UBS sales desk (Rebecca Cheong) expects the current systematic selling to be sharp but last only a day or two. Market internals are better than last Friday's.
Excess buy flow was +$15 bn despite SPX -1.0%. Nasdaq excess sell flow was only -$16 bn against a QQQ move of -2.1%, which is small for a move that size.
Retail bought the dip from 10:30am, with net flow at the 66th percentile vs 3Y. The buy tilt was in ETFs and Tech (Semis and Hardware).
The QQQ drawdown this morning was CTA triggered, around 10-11am. Two NQ1 sell triggers were crossed, pre-open and at 10:27am.
Further CTA selling is possible. ES1 has 6 sell triggers within -2.0% and NQ1 has 3 within -2.0%. RTY1 has no close sell trigger.
Leveraged ETPs are estimated to sell $21.7 bn today, of which $20.1 bn is in NDX + Tech. The split is $11.1 bn Semis, $6.1 bn QQQ, $746 mn MAG-7 and $2.1 bn rest of tech.
Leveraged ETP AUM has fallen to $139 bn (58th percentile vs 5Y). Rebalance sensitivity is now $7.2 bn per 1% underlyer move.

Risk control selling is small at the current move. SPX -1.04% against a daily breakeven of 57 bps implies $20-30 bn to sell, about $5-10 bn today and $15-20 bn tomorrow. Meaningful selling only starts if SPX falls 2% today.
There is no sign of a risk parity unwind today, and barely any this month.
Equity/bond correlation has turned negative again (1M correlation -20%, first negative reading since March). Treasuries work as a risk-off hedge and as diversification again.
VIX is 18.8 and the VIX Cross-Asset Rank is benign at 43%. The VIX/SPX Hi-Low ratio is 2.3x vs 4.1x on Friday, when equity hedging anxiety was not matched by equity moves.
SPX dealer gamma is flat today, between -$8 bn and +$5 bn across 7200-8200. Yesterday it turned long gamma at +$36 bn around 2:50pm, against under +$5 bn long at the open.

sector_views.rationale: Retail is buying the dip in Semis and Hardware. Leveraged ETP rebalancing is concentrated in NDX and Tech, led by Semis, so near-term forced selling pressure is highest there.

risk_factors: Further CTA selling if SPX and NQ1 break the nearby sell triggers.
Leveraged ETP selling concentrated in QQQ and Tech, especially Semis.
Risk control selling becomes meaningful only if SPX falls about 2% or more today. The scenario at -2.5% implies up to $200-280 bn of selling.
The size of the systematic selling depends on how much risk control has to sell.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 18.8 with a VIX Cross-Asset Rank of 43%, which is benign.
VIX/SPX intraday Hi-Low ratio is 2.3x today vs 4.1x on Friday, when option activity was panicked.
SPX dealer gamma is flat. It is between -$8 bn and +$5 bn across 7200-8200, after reaching +$36 bn long around 2:50pm yesterday.
ES1 exposure is at the 71st percentile vs 3Y, NQ1 at the 32nd and RTY1 at the 10th.
NQ1 close sell triggers left: 29035 (ST, -1.0%), 28961 (LT, -1.2%), 28896 (MT, -1.4%). The next one is -2.7% away.
RTY1 has no close sell trigger and one close buy trigger at 2811.9 (ST, +0.8%).
Leveraged ETP sells as a % of ADV are highest in Semis: NXPI 50.8%, ADI 43.5%, MPWR 41.8%, MCHP 35.0%, TXN 34.2%, TER 33.3%, QCOM 26.1%, KLAC 26.1%, ON 20.8%, AEM 19.9%.
Largest leveraged ETP sells in dollars: NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, INTC, AAPL, MSFT, MRVL, TXN and ADI.

Risk control scenarios: SPX -1.5% means $65-85 bn to sell ($20-30 bn today, $40-55 bn tomorrow). SPX -2% means $135-180 bn ($45-60 bn today, $90-120 bn tomorrow). SPX -2.5% means $200-280 bn ($60-80 bn today, $140-200 bn tomorrow).
